comparator.name: Media and Information
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 UvA curriculum and course catalogue, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 course catalogue confirms a 180-EC, English-taught programme. Year 1 is a shared 60-EC media-studies foundation. From Year 2 the programme requires one of two 36-EC specialisations alongside 24 EC of digital methods and philosophy; the neutral official-order rule selects Cultural Information Studies, the first listed route, rather than optimising for UCR fit. Year 3 contains 42 EC of genuine free choice and an 18-EC research seminar and bachelor thesis. Zero-credit literacy, tutoring and writing requirements are excluded from the 180-EC component total.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, ten courses remove advanced coding, AI and data analysis and add rhetoric, audience methods, organisational psychology, leadership, market research, digital transformation and politics. alternativeSelection.assessment: Three defensible, feasible and materially distinct UCR curricula are included: a balanced closest match plus the two official UvA specialisation directions. Further variants would recombine the same media, digital-methods and cultural-analysis evidence after the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Machine Learning is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Digital Methods and Information Analytics, while differing in institutional scope and format.
Introduction to Programming is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Introduction to Digital Humanities, while differing in institutional scope and format.
Database Management Systems is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Coding the Humanities, while differing in institutional scope and format.
Neural Networks & Deep Learning is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Data-Driven Research & Digital Humanities Lab, while differing in institutional scope and format.
Introduction to Film & Media is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Living Information, while differing in institutional scope and format.
Media Archaeology is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Analysing Digital Culture, while differing in institutional scope and format.
Media & the Environment is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Media Culture in Transformation, while differing in institutional scope and format.
The Art of Rhetorical Communication is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Doing Media Studies 1, while differing in institutional scope and format.
Style & Meaning is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Doing Media Studies 2, while differing in institutional scope and format.
World Myth & Literature is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Current Themes in Media Studies, while differing in institutional scope and format.

notes.text: UvA has more dedicated digital-media, platform, archival and digital-humanities coursework than UCR. The UCR alternatives combine relevant courses across media, communication, computing, data science, humanities and social science; they are coherent approximations rather than claims of course equivalence. The selected UvA route also retains 42 EC of genuine free choice, which is not used to invent fixed comparator content or improve apparent overlap.
